cases.event: One summer, many of the fictional corals at {E} turned pale white.
cases.q: What most likely caused the corals at {E} to turn pale?
restate: The corals at {E} turned pale, and the question asks why.
Something caused the corals at {E} to lose their color one summer.
cases.answer: Unusually warm water most likely caused the corals at {E} to turn pale, because the heat made them lose the algae that give them color.
cases.sum: the evidence points to the unusually warm water as the reason the corals turned pale.
cases.myth: The corals at {E} turned pale because the fish painted them white.
cases.mythClause: only the corals near boats turned pale
cases.altText: Some visitors suggested that pollution from a nearby river had damaged the corals at {E}.
cases.patternQ: What pattern connects the water temperature and the color of the corals at {E}?
cases.patternA: The corals turned pale while the water was unusually warm and regained their color after the water cooled, so their color followed the temperature.
cases.patternSum: the corals turned pale while the water was warm and regained their color after the water cooled.

prediction.text: At the start of summer, a visitor predicted that the corals closest to the river at {E} would turn pale first.
prediction.claim: the corals closest to the river at {E} would turn pale first
prediction.whyNot: corals near the river and far from it turned pale at the same rate

cases.observerNote: The divers photographed the same corals every week.

obs.text: Water temperatures at {E} stayed about {n0} degrees Celsius warmer than usual for six weeks.
exps: water that stays warmer than usual for weeks can stress corals until they lose their algae
the corals turned pale during a long warm spell, which fits a heat explanation
six weeks of warmer water is long enough to stress the corals

obs.text: Under a microscope, the pale corals had far fewer of the tiny algae that normally live inside them.
exps: corals get their color from their algae, so losing the algae makes them pale
this shows how the heat turned the corals pale, since stressed corals lose their algae
the missing algae explain the pale color directly

obs.text: When the water cooled in the fall, many of the corals at {E} regained their color within about {n1} weeks.
exps: the corals recovered once the water cooled, which is what would happen if heat were the cause
the color came back when the heat went away, so the two are linked
once the cause faded, the effect faded too

obs.text: Corals near the river mouth and corals far from it turned pale at the same rate.
obs.tag: the corals near and far from the river
exps: if river pollution were the cause, corals near the river would have been hit harder
this rules out the river, because distance from it made no difference
an even pattern across the lagoon fits warm water better than a pollution source in one spot
predExps: this directly contradicts the prediction, since the corals near the river were not the first to turn pale
if the corals closest to the river turned pale first, they would show more damage, but they did not
the prediction expected a difference by distance that never appeared

obs.text: Water tests at {E} found no more pollution than usual.
exps: pollution cannot explain the damage if there was no extra pollution in the water
this rules out pollution, because the tests found normal water
with normal water quality, the pollution explanation has nothing to stand on
